summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and GERD was admitted for fevers and myalgias. He presented with a temperature of 101°F and diffuse muscle pain, likely due to an influenza-like illness. Given his immunosuppressed state, he was started on empiric Tamiflu. Initial labs showed elevated liver enzymes, which persisted despite resolution of fever. Blood and urine cultures were negative, and imaging showed no acute findings. A liver biopsy revealed mild acute cellular rejection, prompting an increase in sirolimus from 2 mg to 3 mg daily. His symptoms resolved, and he was discharged home with plans for follow-up labs, an MRCP, and hepatitis B vaccination. During admission, he was also diagnosed with type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.7%) and advised on dietary management.
problems: Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
